Jerkass Has a Point: Although Matt's desire to defend only the innocent and less wealthy is admirable, given how many rich clients they pass up and how little money they make, it's understandable Foggy doesn't share his compassion. Foggy is also correct that guilty people are also entitled to representation, and it is not a lawyer's job to judge, only to advocate. Shipper on Deck: Even though he jokes Matt should marry Elektra right away for her money, he shows genuine worry for Matt's quick relationship with her and expresses sympathyfor her death.

characters.name: Wesley Owen Welch
characters.description: Kingpin's right-hand man. Alliterative Name:Wesley OwenWelch. Canon Immigrant: He would eventually make his way to the mainstream comics in 2018, as Fisk's Mayoral Chief of Staff. Expy: Of James Wesley, who was Fisk's right-hand man in the comics. It becomes a case ofExpy Coexistencewhen he makes his comic debut in 2018. Non-Action Guy: He doesn't like taking part in the action.

characters.name: Jose Quesada
characters.description: A despicable criminal who runs afoul of Daredevil. Asshole Victim: His death is brutal but nonetheless warranted. Canon Foreigner: He has no direct comic counterpart. Dies Wide Open: We see a shot of his blank eyes before it, along with the remains of his cadaver, is covered up with a body sheet. Half the Man He Used to Be: How he dies, courtesy of a subway train.

characters.name: Dante Jackson
characters.description: An ex-criminal on charge for the murder of Lisa Tazio. Canon Foreigner: He is created exclusively for the director's cut of the film.

characters.name: Old Man
characters.description: An old man who is helped by a young Matt. Abled in the Adaptation: Assuming he is intended to be the old blind man whom Matt Murdock saved in the source material's origin story, he can at least see in this version. The problem is that he is a bit clueless. Ambiguous Situation: Given thatDeadpool & Wolverinehas established these films as part of the same multiverse as the MCU, he may or may not be the same entity asthe Watcher Informant. Creator Cameo: One of Smilin' Stan'smany trademarks. He appears as a clueless man whom a young and blind Matt Murdock saves from being run over while he is too focused on reading his newspaper while walking down the street. Mythology Gag: While not confirmed, it's possible that this character's cameo is a reference to how Matt Murdock was blinded in the comic books when he prevented the truck with the chemicals which blinded him from running over a blind old man.

characters.name: Mark Miller
characters.description: Alliterative Name:MarkMiller. Canon Foreigner: He and his daughter are created specifically for theElektramovie.

characters.name: Abby Miller
characters.description: A girl whom Elektra protects from the Hand. Canon Foreigner: She and her father are created specifically for theElektramovie. Incompletely Trained: Due to being chased by the Hand she's been trained to defend herself. That said, she clearly isn't even on Elektra's level during the first film (in which Elektra was soundly defeated by Bullseye). Morality Pet: Her friendship with Elektra helps her begin to soften up. Obfuscating Stupidity: She actually has combat skills (though nowhere near Elektra's level even in the first film) despite herTroubled Teenexterior.

characters.name: Kirigi
characters.description: Roshi's son and a member of the Hand. Big Bad: Even though he serves his father, Kirigi is the leader of the group from the Hand that's coming for Abby, making him the more active villain. Contrasting Sequel Antagonist: He's a killer for hire like Bullseye. Bullseye was bald, wore a leather black longcoat, had impeccable aiming skills and found Elektra beautiful while hitting with almost sexual delight. Kirigi has long hair, a white Gi, relies on both mystical speed and his swords, and doesn't show an interest in Elektra yet had no problem taunting her.They also each killed one of her parents, though Elektra at least avenges her mother while Bullseye is still out there, albeit unable to do anything but talk and likely has no idea she's come back to life. Final Boss: He's the last foe Elektra faces, and their fight is the final one in this short-lived cinematic universe.

characters.name: Roshi
characters.description: The leader of The Hand. Contrasting Sequel Antagonist: To the Kingpin. Unlike Fisk, he never gets involved in the fight and his ties to Elektra are near non-existent. Greater-Scope Villain: He has clear authority overKirigibut he barely factors into the plot. The Unfought: He never gets involved in a fight with Elektra.

characters.name: Typhoid
characters.description: A member of the Hand. Adaptational Superpower Change: She's has aTouch of Deathinstead of the telepathy, telekinesis, and pyrokinesis of the comics. Kiss of Death: She attempts to poison Elektra with a sudden kiss. Elektra is cured before the poison could do that. Post-Final Boss: After Elektra defeats Kirigi, she decides to deal with Typhoid. She doesn't so much fight as she does throw her sai through the hedge maze, with Typhoid barely having time to realize what happened before she's stabbed through the face. Race Lift: Typhoid Mary in the comics is Caucasain. Here, she's played by half-MalaysianNatassia Malthe.

characters.name: DeMarco
characters.description: A criminal who runs afoul of Elektra. Starter Villain: Not counting her fight with and humiliating defeat by Bullseye,DeMarcois the first target Elektra comes after.
